findings.description: The security group allows TCP port 22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or exploit attempts against the instance.

findings.issue_category: hardcoded cloud credentials in user data
findings.description: The user_data script exports a static AWS access key ID and secret access key. EC2 user data is readable by anyone who can reach the instance metadata service (and by any user on the host), leaking long-lived credentials.

No metadata_options block requiring http_tokens = "required" is set, so IMDSv1 remains enabled and SSRF against the web server could be used to read instance metadata and any attached role credentials.
The instance does not define root_block_device with encrypted = true, so the root volume data is stored unencrypted at rest.
The EBS volume is created without encrypted = true or a KMS key, leaving attached data and any snapshots unencrypted at rest.
The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted EBS volume, so the backup copy of the data is also unencrypted and could be exposed if the snapshot is shared or leaked.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption and public access controls
findings.description: The VPC flow log bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, no public access block, no versioning, and no enforced TLS-only bucket policy, so sensitive network telemetry is stored unencrypted and is at risk of accidental public exposure.

findings.issue_category: force destroy enabled on log bucket
findings.description: force_destroy = true allows the audit/flow-log bucket and all its contents to be deleted without emptying it first, letting an attacker or accidental apply destroy forensic evidence.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance launched in this subnet to receive a public IP, directly exposing workloads to the internet rather than placing them behind a NAT/load balancer.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true gives all instances in this subnet public IP addresses, increasing the internet-facing attack surface.
The egress rule permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, allowing a compromised instance unrestricted outbound connectivity for command-and-control traffic or data exfiltration.
The instance serves content over plain HTTP on port 80 open to the world, with no TLS termination, so any traffic to the portal is transmitted in cleartext.
